problem_statement: When a dual-stack (IPv6) UDP socket sends a datagram via sendto() or sendmsg() to a destination that is an IPv4 address expressed as an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (for example ::ffff:127.0.0.1), the send is treated as an IPv6 send instead of an IPv4 send. As a result the datagram is not delivered to the IPv4 peer: a datagram sent back to an IPv4 client that previously connected through the dual-stack server is lost, and the client does not receive the echoed data. Sending to such a mapped address must be recognised as an IPv4 send so the packet reaches the IPv4 destination.
